Preparation Tips
Freeze Warning Tonight
Austin, TX · Updated just now
27°F
Tonight's Low
45°F
Today's High
12 hrs
Below Freezing
National Weather Service has issued a Freeze Warning for Travis County from 11 PM tonight through 9 AM tomorrow.
Preparation Tips
Drip outdoor faucets
Let cold and hot water trickle from faucets on exterior walls to prevent pipe freezing.
Open cabinet doors
Open cabinets under sinks on exterior walls to allow warm air to circulate around pipes.
Disconnect garden hoses
Disconnect and drain garden hoses. Cover outdoor spigots with insulated covers.
Keep thermostat above 55°F
Don't lower your thermostat too much overnight — keep it at minimum 55°F even when away.
Protect plants
Cover vulnerable plants with frost cloth or bring potted plants indoors.
Shut off irrigation system
Turn off and drain your irrigation / sprinkler system to prevent cracked lines.

Buyer & Resale Snapshot

Your Energy Profile is valuable for buyers and can be shared as part of your home's transfer package.

  • ✓ Helps buyers understand likely operating costs — transparency builds trust
  • ✓ Highlights upgrades already completed — shows home value and maintenance
  • ✓ Identifies future improvement opportunities — helps estimate lifetime value
  • ✓ Can support listing materials — market energy efficiency as a feature
  • ✓ Can store certified reports for buyer review — all documentation in one place
Visible in Transfer Package: Yes
💡 Private utility bills are never shared unless you choose to include them.

What is FORTIFIED?

FORTIFIED is a nationally recognized construction and retrofit standard that strengthens homes against severe weather, including high winds, hurricanes, and hail, by improving roof systems and structural connections.

Improve Your Home's Strength

Not Certified

The following upgrades can meaningfully improve your resilience score and move your home toward FORTIFIED certification.

HIGH PRIORITY
Roof Decking Attachment Upgrade
Upgrade sheathing fasteners to 8d ring-shank nails at 6" spacing for stronger wind resistance.
Est. Cost: $800–$1,600
Impact: High — Required for FORTIFIED Roof
HIGH PRIORITY
Sealed Roof Deck
Add a secondary water barrier under shingles to prevent water intrusion if shingles are damaged.
Est. Cost: $500–$1,000
Impact: High — Required for FORTIFIED Roof
MEDIUM PRIORITY
Roof-to-Wall Connections
Hurricane straps or clips connect roof framing directly to wall framing, significantly improving uplift resistance.
Est. Cost: $1,500–$3,500
Impact: Medium — Required for FORTIFIED Silver
MEDIUM PRIORITY
Impact-Resistant Shingles
Class 4 impact-resistant shingles provide superior protection from hail and windblown debris.
Est. Cost: $4,000–$9,000
Impact: Medium — Boosts score +8–12
LOW PRIORITY
Secondary Water Barrier
A fully adhered underlayment installed beneath shingles that acts as a second line of defense against water intrusion in high-wind events.
Est. Cost: $600–$1,200 · Impact: Supports FORTIFIED Roof level
ℹ️

Resilience upgrades and certifications like FORTIFIED may improve your home's durability and could become increasingly relevant for insurance, resale, and long-term protection.

How long does the visit take?
Most visits take 90–120 minutes, depending on the size of your home and how much existing documentation (manuals, warranties) you have on hand. You don't need to prepare anything in advance.
What does "vetted" actually mean?
Every HomeHub Setup Assist inspector is background-checked, carries active state licensure where required, holds $1M+ liability insurance, and has passed our platform certification. We re-verify credentials annually.

Frequently Asked Questions

🚀 Getting Started
What is HomeHub and how does it work?
HomeHub is a centralized platform for managing all aspects of your home. It tracks projects, maintenance schedules, contractor information, warranties, insurance documents, and historical records. You can share secure access with contractors via QR codes, track work progress in real-time, confirm final costs, and build a transferable record of your home's history.
How do I get started with HomeHub?
Start by creating an account and adding your property information. Then explore the Dashboard to understand your home systems and view your Home Health Score. Next, add your first project or set up maintenance reminders. You can also book Setup Assist for a professional inspector to create a comprehensive baseline of your home.
What do I need to set up HomeHub?
All you need is a valid email address and basic information about your property (address, year built, square footage). You can start with minimal information and add details over time as you complete projects or log maintenance work.
📋 Projects & Tracking
How do I add a new project?
Navigate to the Projects section and click "+ New Project". Enter the project name, description, budget, timeline, and select or add a contractor. You can upload photos, documents, and specifications. Once created, you can share the project with your contractor via a secure QR code.
Can I track multiple projects at once?
Yes! HomeHub allows you to manage unlimited projects simultaneously. Organize them by status (Current, Past, Future) or by category to keep track of everything. Each project has its own timeline, budget, contractor information, and documentation.
What is cost confirmation and why is it important?
After a project is completed, you and the contractor confirm the final cost paid. This is separate from payment processing—it's about documenting actual expenses for your records. Once both parties confirm the final cost, you can both leave reviews. This ensures transparency and creates an accurate financial history of your home maintenance.
🔧 Contractors & Access
How do I share access with contractors?
Go to your project and find the Contractor Access section. Display or share the QR code with your contractor. They can scan it to instantly gain secure access to that specific project. You control what information they can see and when their access expires. This gives contractors real-time project updates without sharing your entire home data.
Can I revoke contractor access anytime?
Yes, absolutely. You have complete control over contractor access. You can revoke access at any time from the Active Contractors list. Once revoked, the contractor can no longer view project information. All access history is tracked for your records.
How do I find and vet contractors?
Use the Contractor Phone Book to browse vetted professionals in your area. View ratings, reviews, completed work, and specialties. You can also add contractors from your network or previous projects to your personal list for easy reference.
❤️ Home Health & Maintenance
What is the Home Health Score?
Your Home Health Score is a calculated metric (0-100) that reflects the overall condition of your home's major systems. It's based on age, maintenance history, recent repairs, and system status. A higher score indicates better condition and may help reduce insurance costs. You can improve your score through regular maintenance and timely repairs.
How do I set up maintenance reminders?
Navigate to Maintenance Calendar and add recurring tasks for your home systems. Set frequency (monthly, quarterly, annually), and HomeHub will send you alerts before maintenance is due. You can also set weather-triggered alerts for tasks like winterization or storm preparation.
How do I track warranties on my home systems?
Upload warranty documents in the Documents section or add warranty details when logging completed work. HomeHub will automatically alert you when warranties are approaching expiration so you don't miss important coverage deadlines. All warranty information is organized by system and project.
💰 Pricing & Setup Assist
Does the $249 really include a year of Premium?
Yes. Your first year of HomeHub Premium ($14.99/mo value) is bundled into the $249 price for new members. You'll be asked about renewal 30 days before the year ends — no auto-charge surprises.
Is Setup Assist worth the cost?
Most homeowners find it valuable because it saves 6-10 hours of work locating information and creates an accurate baseline for your home's condition. The professional inspection identifies issues early, your documented records can reduce insurance costs, and the Resale Dossier can add significant value if you sell.
I'm already a subscriber—why is it cheaper?
Since you already pay for HomeHub, we remove the bundled first-year cost. Active subscribers pay a reduced rate for the on-site Setup Assist visit.
🔒 Security & Privacy
Is my information secure?
Yes. HomeHub uses industry-standard encryption to protect your personal and property information. Contractor access is controlled through unique QR codes that can be revoked at any time. You have complete control over what information is visible to whom. We never share your data with third parties without your explicit consent.
Can I integrate insurance information?
Yes. You can upload insurance documents, policy details, and agent information. HomeHub will track policy expiration dates and help you manage claims by linking them to specific projects. Some insurance providers offer premium discounts for homes with documented maintenance records like HomeHub provides.
What happens to my data if I delete my account?
All your personal data, projects, documents, and records are permanently deleted within 30 days of account deletion. We retain no backups of your information. You can export your data before deletion if needed.
🏠 Selling & Transferring Your Home
Can I export my home records for selling?
Yes! The Resale Dossier feature compiles all your home's documentation, project history, maintenance records, and contractor information into a professional package. This can be invaluable when selling your home as it demonstrates maintenance history and builds buyer confidence. You can customize what's included before sharing.
How do I transfer my property to a new owner?
Use the Transfer Property feature to securely hand over your property record to the next homeowner. They verify their identity and you have a 48-hour review window to cancel if needed. Private documents like insurance files can be withheld during transfer.
What information shows in my Resale Dossier?
Your Resale Dossier includes completed projects, maintenance history, Home Health Score, system inspections, warranties still in effect, contractor reviews, and project photos. You control exactly what's included and can exclude sensitive information before sharing with buyers or their agents.

Have More Questions?

Didn't find your answer? Send us your question and we'll get back to you as soon as possible. This is not a live help line, but we do our best to respond promptly.

⏱️ Response Time: We typically respond within 24-48 business hours. For urgent issues, please call our support line.

Home Instructions

💧

Water Shutoff

Step-by-step instructions to locate and turn off your main water supply in an emergency.

Emergency Utilities
Added
Jan 10, 2025

Instructions:

  1. Locate the main water shutoff valve. It's typically found in the basement, crawlspace, or utility room near the water meter or where the main line enters your home.
  2. Turn the valve clockwise. Use a wrench or valve key if needed. Turn slowly but firmly until you feel resistance.
  3. Test to confirm water is off. Open a faucet in your home. If no water flows, the shutoff was successful.
  4. If water still flows, there may be a secondary shutoff valve at the water meter. Call a plumber if you cannot locate it.

Important Notes:

  • Know where your shutoff valve is located before an emergency occurs.
  • Test your shutoff valve annually to ensure it works smoothly.
  • Keep the area around your shutoff valve clear and accessible.
  • If the valve is stuck or won't turn, call a professional plumber immediately.
🌬️

HVAC Filter Replacement

How to replace your HVAC system's air filters every 3 months to maintain efficiency and air quality.

Maintenance Equipment
Added
Dec 20, 2024

What You'll Need:

  • Replacement air filter (check your system manual for correct size and MERV rating)
  • Ladder (if filter is located high)

Steps:

  1. Turn off your HVAC system. This prevents dust from circulating while the filter compartment is open.
  2. Locate the filter. It's usually in a return air duct or blower compartment. Check your manual if unsure.
  3. Note the filter size and direction. Filters have an arrow showing airflow direction. Replace with the same size and direction.
  4. Remove the old filter. Slide it out carefully to avoid dropping dust.
  5. Insert the new filter. Ensure the arrow points toward your furnace/system (away from return air).
  6. Turn your HVAC system back on. Your system is now running efficiently with a fresh filter.

Replacement Schedule:

  • Every 3 months: Standard 1–3 inch filters with normal use
  • Every 6 months: High-MERV or thick filters
  • More often if: You have pets, allergies, or live in a dusty area
⚡

Generator Startup

Quick start guide for your backup generator with critical safety precautions for power outages.

Emergency Equipment
Added
Nov 5, 2024
⚠️ CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING
Always place your generator outside in open air. Generators produce carbon monoxide, which is deadly if inhaled. Never run inside your home, garage, basement, or crawlspace. Position at least 20 feet away from doors and windows.

Pre-Startup Checklist:

  • Check fuel level and add fuel if needed (use only fresh, clean fuel)
  • Ensure oil level is adequate (check dipstick)
  • Verify all connections are secure and dry
  • Load level is appropriate (don't exceed generator capacity)

Startup Steps:

  1. Move generator outside. Position it at least 20 feet from doors, windows, and vents.
  2. Set the fuel valve to "ON". Locate on the fuel line.
  3. Set the choke to "COLD". (Skip if your generator has automatic choke)
  4. Turn the ignition key to "ON". Do NOT start yet.
  5. Pull the starter cord or press electric start. Engine should turn over.
  6. Let engine warm up for 2–3 minutes before connecting loads.
  7. Set choke to "WARM" once engine is running smoothly.
  8. Connect devices one at a time. Start with essential loads (refrigerator, lights, medical equipment).

Shutdown Steps:

  1. Turn off all connected devices first.
  2. Wait 2–3 minutes to let engine cool slightly.
  3. Set choke to "COLD".
  4. Turn ignition key to "OFF".
  5. Set fuel valve to "OFF".

Transfer Property

Transfer your property record(s) to the next homeowner(s)

About This Transfer
The buyer will verify their identity after you initiate. There's a 48-hour review window where you can cancel. Private documents like insurance files won't transfer.
Step 1 — Choose a Transfer Mode
🏠
One at a Time
Transfer one property to one buyer. Repeat for each property.
📦
Block Transfer
Transfer multiple properties to the same buyer in one action.
🔀
Split Transfer
Transfer multiple properties to different buyers — each assigned separately.
Select the property to transfer:
Buyer Information
Select properties to transfer together:
Buyer Information — all selected properties go to this buyer
Select each property and assign it to a buyer. Each property can go to a different recipient.

What Gets Transferred

✓ INCLUDED
  • Maintenance history
  • Equipment details
  • Contractor records
  • Service photos
  • Warranties
✕ PRIVATE
  • Insurance policies
  • Payment history
  • Personal notes
  • Financial docs
  • Private uploads
